note: Secret + var CONTRACT for the Workhorse worker. Declares what exists, who needs it, and what breaks without it. NEVER contains values. Verify with: bun run secrets

core.description: The fleet cannot run without these.

browser.description: Sandbox callback credential for the /browser endpoint.

slack.description: Slack operator surface. Needs BOTH values — one alone is a half-wired surface that accepts events it cannot reply to.

jira.description: Jira intake surface. Needs the full set — a webhook with no API token receives issues it cannot transition.

ntfy.description: Push notifications. URL + topic are required together; token only for protected topics.

search.description: Web search providers. Any subset works — the chain skips unset providers.

flags.description: Rollout and behavior flags. Not secret — plain config.

entries.name: SPIKE_TOKEN
entries.purpose: Master bearer token gating every /api route and the UI's server-side calls.
entries.withoutIt: Every API request 401s. The UI, CLI, and chat surface cannot reach the fleet at all.

entries.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
entries.purpose: Clones repos into ticket sandboxes, pushes branches, opens PRs, and backs every gh_* read tool through the scoped worker proxy.
entries.withoutIt: No ticket can clone, push, or open a PR — the whole coding pipeline is inert.
entries.obtain: https://github.com/settings/tokens — classic PAT with repo scope, or a fine-grained token with Contents + Pull requests write.

entries.name: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.purpose: HMAC-verifies POST /webhooks/github deliveries (PR review feedback, CI results).
entries.withoutIt: Webhook deliveries are rejected, so PR feedback never reaches the therapist stage and revision runs never trigger.
entries.obtain: Generate one, then paste the same value into the GitHub webhook config: openssl rand -hex 32

entries.name: SELF_URL
entries.purpose: This Worker's own public URL, so ticket sandboxes can call back to POST /browser.
entries.withoutIt: Sandbox-side tools cannot reach the worker; browser and callback tools fail.
entries.obtain: The deployed workers.dev URL or custom domain. Lives in wrangler.jsonc vars — NOT a secret, it is public by definition.

entries.name: BROWSER_TOKEN
entries.purpose: Scoped token injected into ticket sandboxes for the /browser endpoint, so untrusted repo code never sees SPIKE_TOKEN.
entries.withoutIt: Sandboxes fall back to no browser callback. Worst case if LEAKED: someone can read the fleet, not command it — which is the entire reason it is separate from SPIKE_TOKEN.

entries.name: IMGBB_KEY
entries.purpose: Primary image host for PR embeds. Injected into the sandbox's imgup config at prepare so upload_image tries the keyed host first.
entries.withoutIt: upload_image silently falls back to the keyless hosts (imgbox/pixhost/catbox), which throttle datacenter IPs — PR screenshots become unreliable rather than broken.

entries.name: OPENCODE_API_KEY
entries.purpose: opencode subscription key. Powers the model-eval harness (opencode-go, flat rate) and is the intended home for a validated fallback model leg.
entries.withoutIt: bun run eval:tools self-skips. No effect on production runs today, since the stage leg chain is Anthropic-only.

entries.name: SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET
entries.purpose: Verifies POST /webhooks/slack deliveries.
entries.withoutIt: The Slack surface is disabled.
entries.obtain: Slack app settings → Basic Information → Signing Secret.

entries.name: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
entries.purpose: Posts replies and status updates back to Slack threads.
entries.withoutIt: The Slack surface is disabled.
entries.obtain: Slack app → OAuth & Permissions → Bot User OAuth Token. Needs app_mentions:read, chat:write, and the message.channels event subscription.

entries.name: JIRA_BASE_URL
entries.purpose: Jira instance base URL, e.g. https://yourorg.atlassian.net.
entries.withoutIt: The Jira surface is disabled.
entries.obtain: Your Atlassian cloud URL. Not secret.

entries.name: JIRA_EMAIL
entries.purpose: Account email paired with the API token for basic auth.
entries.withoutIt: The Jira surface is disabled.
entries.obtain: The Atlassian account email. Not secret on its own, but useless without the token.

entries.name: JIRA_API_TOKEN
entries.purpose: Outbound Jira transitions and comments.
entries.withoutIt: The Jira surface is disabled.

entries.name: JIRA_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.purpose: Required as ?secret= on /webhooks/jira. Atlassian cloud webhooks cannot sign requests, so a query-string shared secret is the only available check.
entries.withoutIt: The Jira surface is disabled.
entries.obtain: Generate one, then append it to the webhook URL in Jira: openssl rand -hex 32

entries.name: JIRA_AGENT_ACCOUNT
entries.purpose: The agent's accountId/email/displayName — marks which assignee triggers intake and filters the bot's own comment echoes.
entries.withoutIt: Without it the bot can react to its own comments, looping.
entries.obtain: The Jira account used by the bot. Not secret.

entries.name: NTFY_URL
entries.purpose: ntfy server base URL — self-hosted or https://ntfy.sh.
entries.withoutIt: Push notifications are disabled.

entries.name: NTFY_TOPIC
entries.purpose: Topic to publish to.
entries.withoutIt: Push notifications are disabled.
entries.obtain: Any topic name. Treat as secret-ish on public ntfy.sh, where the topic name IS the access control.

entries.name: NTFY_TOKEN
entries.purpose: Bearer token for protected topics.
entries.withoutIt: Fine for public topics; protected topics reject publishes.

entries.name: TRIGGER_SECRET
entries.purpose: Shared secret for POST /triggers/:name/fire (webhook-style trigger firing).
entries.withoutIt: Webhook-fired triggers are unavailable; cron triggers still work.

entries.name: SEARCH_PROVIDER
entries.purpose: Default web-search provider: tavily | exa | brave.
entries.withoutIt: The chain picks the first provider that has a key.

entries.name: JINA_API_KEY
entries.purpose: Jina Reader — backs web_read (page to clean markdown).
entries.withoutIt: web_read fails; agents must fall back to the real browser, which is far more expensive.

entries.name: TAVILY_API_KEY
entries.purpose: Tavily web search.
entries.withoutIt: Tavily is skipped in the provider chain.

entries.name: EXA_API_KEY
entries.purpose: Exa web search.
entries.withoutIt: Exa is skipped in the provider chain.

entries.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
entries.purpose: Brave web search.
entries.withoutIt: Brave is skipped in the provider chain.

entries.name: FLUE_STAGES
entries.purpose: Comma-separated workflow names (or "all") whose stages run via the in-process flue harness instead of the pi subprocess.
entries.withoutIt: Defaults to the pi path.
entries.obtain: Set to "all" once the flue path is validated. Not secret — and being a secret today means its value cannot be read back to debug a rollout.
